chunks: Muḥammad ibn Muslim and Zurārah ibn Aʿyan asked Abū Jaʿfar al-Bāqir عليه السلام about fasting on the Day of ʿĀshūrāʾ, and he said:
"Its fasting was observed before the month of Ramaḍān; then when the month of Ramaḍān was revealed, it was abandoned."

key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramaḍān, during which obligatory fasting was prescribed
key_terms.صَوْمِ: fasting; the act of abstaining in worship
key_terms.عَاشُورَاءَ: ʿĀshūrāʾ; the tenth day of Muḥarram
key_terms.يَوْمِ: day; indicating the specific occasion under discussion

ai.seo_question: Was fasting on the Day of ʿĀshūrāʾ still practiced after Ramaḍān became obligatory?
ai.summary: This hadith states that fasting on the Day of ʿĀshūrāʾ had been practiced before the obligation of fasting in Ramaḍān. After Ramaḍān was instituted, that earlier practice was left aside. The narration is significant for understanding the historical development of fasting rulings in early Islam.
